Jake: Bro, heard you on Love Online last night.
Peter: Ugh. How big of a moron did I sound like?
Jake: Dude. You sound like you've got it pretty bad for this girl. Pretty intense dude. Tomorrow at this time, you will have been wining and dining SWEET GIRL for over an hour.
Peter: Tomorrow at this time, I will have been eating a big bowl of shame and embarrassment for over an hour. With a side order of bitter tears.

Jake: You're hanging from a pretty small thread my friend, but going forward, you won't have to worry about that.
Peter: No?
Jake: No, tomorrow is an opportunity. You have to seize every moment. This is just a chapter in your life. Dude. You don't have to be crazy, but you do have to take some risks otherwise, you never grow.
Peter: I'm so worried about tomorrow night. By tomorrow, I will have been worrying about this for the better part of a week.
Jake: Understandable, but tomorrow night you don't need be scared, you must be courageous. Tomorrow, you don't need to be worried because you have nothing to lose and everything to gain. I admire what you are doing here man. You are taking a chance.

Peter: Really?
Jake: For sure. Next year, at this time, you and your lady love will have been dating for over a year and everyone will be clamoring to hear your story. Before you get married, you will have been telling that tale over and over, because people love stories of happy endings and true love. In fact you have inspired me to do a little online dating myself. I was wondering if you could help me set up a profile right now.
Peter: Sure. First thing, you don't have to put your real name on your profile. In fact, you shouldn't.
What does Jake include in his profile?

Future Perfect Continuous: Duration and Cause
You use the Future Perfect Continuous tense to talk about an action in the future that is unfinished at the time another action in the future starts.

When you use the Future Perfect Continuous, you can sometimes think of it as the Present Perfect Continuous, but instead of your viewpoint being in the present, it is in the future.
With the Future Perfect Continuous, an action in the future is unfinished by the time another action in the future starts. It is most often used with an expression of time.
The Future Perfect Continuous is used to express duration and cause.
Structure:</br> subject + will have been + present participle

Example:

Tomorrow at this time, you will have been wining and dining SWEETGIRL for over an hour.

You will have been telling that tale over and over by the time you get married, because people love happy endings.
Next year, at this time, you and your lady love will have been dating for over a year.
Before you get married, you will have been telling that tale  over and over, because people love stories of happy endings and true love.
By tomorrow, I will have been worrying about this for the better part of a week.
Expressing Absence of Necessity in the Future
You use the negative forms of the modals need to and have to to express absence of necessity in the future.

Absence of necessity is expressed with the negative form of have to, not with mustn't.
Example:
    You don't have to date her if you don't like her. (it is not necessary to date her)
    You mustn't date her. (it is necessary not to date her)

Absence of necessity can also be expressed by the negative form of need.

To express absence of necessity in the future, you use the structure: subject + won't + have/need + infinitive.
Example:
You won't have to worry about online dating once you get married.

If you set up your online profile properly, you won't need to sift through tons of irrelevant messages.
Going forward, you won't have to worry about that.
You don't have to be crazy, but you do have to take some risks otherwise, you never grow.
First thing, you don't have to put your real name on your profile.
Tomorrow, you don't need to be worried because you have nothing to lose and everything to gain.
